cards.name: Adobe PDF Presets...
cards.summary: Opens the Adobe PDF Presets dialog, where the named PDF export settings (.joboptions files shared by the Creative Cloud apps, e.g. [High Quality Print], [Press Quality], [PDF/X-4:2008], [Smallest File Size]) are created, edited, deleted, imported and exported. It manages presets only; it does not save a PDF. Enabled with no document open.
cards.how: Pick a preset to read its summary, then New or Edit to set compatibility, PDF/X standard, compression, marks and bleeds and output colour; Import / Export move .joboptions files between machines or from a print shop. The built-in presets (in square brackets) cannot be edited, only copied with New.
use_for: setting up a print shop's PDF/X preset once so every brochure, poster and packaging file exports the same way
making a small-file web/email PDF preset for client proofs
importing the .joboptions a printer sent so Illustrator, Photoshop and InDesign all export to their spec
avoid: exporting the document itself: use File > Save As (Adobe PDF) and pick the preset there
editing a built-in preset expecting it to change: duplicate it with New and edit the copy

cards.name: Assign Profile...
cards.summary: Opens the Assign Profile dialog for the active document: choose Don't Color Manage This Document, the current working space, or any installed ICC profile. Assigning changes how the document's colour numbers are interpreted on screen and in output; the numbers themselves are not converted. Needs an open document.
cards.how: Choose one of three options: Don't Color Manage This Document, Working RGB/CMYK (the space from Color Settings), or Profile (pick from the list). The profile is embedded when the file is saved with Embed ICC Profiles on.
use_for: tagging a client's untagged CMYK logo file with the press profile it was built for
checking how the same CMYK numbers look under a different press profile (coated vs uncoated)
fixing a file opened with the wrong profile so colours preview correctly
avoid: converting colours to a new press condition: assigning keeps the numbers and only changes the look; convert on export (PDF Output: Convert to Destination) instead
changing the document's colour mode (RGB vs CMYK): use File > Document Color Mode
